notable_absence.finding: No Enterprise/Community edition badge anywhere, and (necessarily, since there is no Capella twin page) no Capella-role content. Every prerequisite on this page is either an RBAC role (Full Admin/Eventing Full Admin, for viewing Application logs) or direct node/filesystem access (editing static_config, copying icudtl.dat, setting up NAT alternate addresses) - there is no privilege catalogue distinct from the role, matching this batch's other RBAC findings.

cross_component_finding: eventing:visual-debugger (minted independently in this batch's eventing-timers.json, which states only 'Timers cannot be debugged using the Visual Debugger') is fully specified here for the first time: a Function-level Debug flag, a default port (9140), a one-time single-mutation debug session, and a native transpiler + source map that lets the debugger show original rather than transpiled code. This page is also the first in the batch to name the actual OS processes/paths behind Eventing's logs (per-platform filesystem paths for eventing.log and the per-Function <name>.log files, and the cbcollect_info/log-rotation/log-redaction machinery), none of which appear on any other page in this batch.
cross_product_finding: Going into this round, this page's lack of a Capella twin was flagged as presumptive evidence that Capella lacks Eventing's interactive debugger. Direct evidence says otherwise: cloud/eventing/eventing-Terminologies.md's own 'Debug' glossary entry describes the identical mechanism in almost the same words - 'The debug operation traps and sends the next event instance received by the Eventing Function to a separate v8 worker with debugging enabled. Debug is a special flag that can be attach to a Function... opens a TCP port, and generates a Chrome Developer Tools URL with a session cookie that can be used to control the debug worker.' So the live Visual Debugger IS a genuine Capella feature, not a Server-only one - the two products differ in DOCUMENTATION STRUCTURE (Capella folds it into a glossary entry; Server gives it a full page with a step-by-step workflow) rather than in capability. What actually IS absent from the entire cloud/eventing/ tree (confirmed by search) is everything on this page that presumes direct node/OS access: modifying the debug port by hand-editing /opt/couchbase/etc/couchbase/static_config and deleting config.dat, the NAT'd-IP alternate-address curl workaround against a literal node IP, and the icudtl.dat file-copy fix for the Chrome ICU disconnect bug (MB-41508). That distinction - not 'Capella has no debugger' but 'Capella's docs describe the debugger's existence without ever exposing the node-administration tasks needed to work around its rough edges' - is the structurally sound version of this round's cross-product finding, and it is only visible by reading the Capella glossary entry rather than trusting the absence of a same-named page.
evidence_provenance: cross-page: the quote confirming Capella documents the same live debugger mechanism is not on server/current/eventing/eventing-debugging-and-diagnosability.md itself; it is the 'Debug' glossary entry on the Capella twin of a different page in this batch (eventing-Terminologies.md), cited here because it directly overturns the premise this page's twin-absence was expected to support.
